findings.title: LayoutLM v1 document-question-answering needs a winml-registered extractive-QA OnnxConfig (Optimum has none) plus hand-tuned input ranges.
findings.observation: impira/layoutlm-invoices is LayoutLMForQuestionAnswering (extractive QA: start_logits/end_logits), loaded via AutoModelForDocumentQuestionAnswering (layoutlm v1 is ONLY in MODEL_FOR_DOCUMENT_QUESTION_ANSWERING_MAPPING_NAMES, not the plain QA mapping). Optimum's TasksManager registers layoutlm only for feature-extraction/fill-mask/text-classification/token-classification, so `winml config -t document-question-answering --model-type layoutlm` FAILS ('layoutlm doesn't support task document-question-answering'). Added src/winml/modelkit/models/hf/layoutlm.py: @register_onnx_overwrite('layoutlm','document-question-answering') on LayoutLMDocumentQAOnnxConfig(LayoutLMOnnxConfig), overriding outputs to {start_logits,end_logits} (Optimum's document-question-answering common output is a single 'logits' tensor, which is WRONG for this extractive head), plus a RoBERTa-style _adjust_position_embeddings (this checkpoint uses a RoBERTa vocab: max_position_embeddings=514, pad_token_id=1 -> usable 512). Wired into hf/__init__.py. fp16 build exit0 in 97.5s; model.onnx.data 242.6MB (half of 485MB fp32); 206 FLOAT16 / 0 FLOAT32 initializers; IN input_ids/bbox/attention_mask/token_type_ids, OUT start_logits/end_logits [1,512]. CPU perf P50 280.62ms (3.56 samples/sec) via --input-data npz.

gotchas: type_vocab_size=1 on this checkpoint: token_type_embeddings has a single row, so token_type_ids MUST be 0. winml's default value_range [0,2] and winml perf's random inputs both emit value 1 -> ONNXRuntime Gather 'indices element out of data bounds' at /layoutlm/embeddings/token_type_embeddings/Gather. Recipe pins token_type_ids value_range to [0,1] (yields 0). Perf must be run with --input-data (npz: token_type_ids=0, bbox=0, input_ids<vocab, attention_mask=1).

max_position_embeddings=514 with pad_token_id=1 (RoBERTa vocab, 50265). winml config resolves sequence_length from the raw config -> emits seq_len 514, which OOBs position embeddings during export ('index out of range in self'). Recipe pins all seq shapes to 512. The code-side _adjust_position_embeddings is defensive (autoconf path) but does NOT change the config-gen shape resolution.
bbox value_range [0,1] resolves to constant 0 (random_(0,1) -> 0); [0,0] errors 'random_ expects from < to'. Constant-0 bbox is safe for tracing (h=w=0 diff -> index 0, no negative index).
Optimum vendor OnnxConfig existing != task registered: LayoutLMOnnxConfig class exists but has no document-question-answering entry in TasksManager. Registration is per-(model_type,task).
feature_gaps_filed: winml value_range resolution ignores type_vocab_size (emits token_type_ids [0,2] even when type_vocab_size=1) -> should clamp to [0, type_vocab_size].
winml perf random input generation ignores model embedding-table bounds (token_type_ids); no way to constrain ranges without a full npz.
findings.mechanism_notes: Confirmed by direct forward pass: model runs with token_type_ids=0 for input_ids up to vocab-1; fails only when token_type_ids hits value 1 (type_vocab_size=1). Export OOB confirmed tied to seq_len 514 vs usable 512.

findings.title: LayoutLMForQuestionAnswering must resolve by architecture to document-question-answering and AutoModelForDocumentQuestionAnswering, not next-sentence-prediction.
findings.observation: On winml 0.2.0 / ORT 1.24.5 at baseline e7509b1e908c74beff0a5655b8f8d7de69c5afae, DmitrySpartak/layoutlm-invoices auto-resolved to next-sentence-prediction and AutoModelForNextSentencePrediction; recipe-free build exited 2 with 'Unrecognized LayoutLMConfig for AutoModelForNextSentencePrediction'. The L1 class-of-models repair maps model_type=layoutlm plus architectures[0]=LayoutLMForQuestionAnswering to document-question-answering, maps that model-type/task pair to AutoModelForDocumentQuestionAnswering, and registers a LayoutLM v1 ONNX config. Explicit and automatic config then agreed and recipe-free fp32/fp16 builds emitted the document-QA contract: input_ids, bbox, attention_mask, token_type_ids -> start_logits, end_logits. The mapping is architecture/task-driven; it contains no checkpoint-ID branch and leaves non-QA LayoutLM heads on their existing Optimum task paths.

findings.title: LayoutLM v1 dummy and semantic inputs must honor embedding-table and document-layout bounds; generic perf must propagate high-exclusive input_value_ranges.
findings.observation: DmitrySpartak/layoutlm-invoices has type_vocab_size=1, so token_type_ids must be zero; bbox coordinates are normalized integer indices in [0,1023], and its RoBERTa-style max_position_embeddings=514 with pad_token_id=1 yields a usable sequence length of 512. The producer repaired the generic adapter so canonical ranges remain high-exclusive while the legacy NumPy integer generator receives an inclusive maximum. Current tester PASS d30aa86fdad717c57096d1b38c7e6a1c04fcb2b4fd16a460b9e39026ca270985 records zero violations for token_type_ids, arbitrary/singleton integer inputs, ranged float input, and unspecified float defaults; default fp32/fp16 perf completed without --input-data. findings.observation: Baseline on origin/main `defa3f63ffdc5c4cd3c252a4b3f60fcc9939f953` failed for `winml build -m impira/layoutlm-document-qa ... --no-analyze --no-optimize --no-quant --no-compile --rebuild` by misrouting the checkpoint to `AutoModelForNextSentencePrediction` / unsupported `LayoutLMConfig`. Historical producer commits were `20ab04a4` and `5bd5ad4b`; the latter renamed an unmaterialized fp16 request to fp32, a repair strategy superseded by current exact-fp16 rebuild requirements.

findings.title: `impira/layoutlm-document-qa` requires all-zero `token_type_ids` because `type_vocab_size=1`; random segment ids crash at the token-type embedding gather
findings.observation: `temp\impira_layoutlm-document-qa\l0_validate.log` records the HF config as `type_vocab_size=1` and the token-type embedding table as shape `[1, 768]`. Raw CLI perf on both artifacts (`temp\impira_layoutlm-document-qa\perf_fp16_cli.log` / `perf_w8a16_cli.log`) then failed with `Gather ... idx=1 must be within the inclusive range [-1,0]`, i.e. random dummy `token_type_ids` hit an out-of-bounds lookup. The historical producer-side fix used `ZeroTokenTypeLayoutLMTextInputGenerator` to force zero-only segment IDs; the current generalized implementation instead uses `LayoutLMTextInputGenerator` with metadata-derived high-exclusive `type_vocab_size`, preserving zero-only generation for this checkpoint and valid multi-type generation for sibling checkpoints. The tester's `_meta-017` fallback harness supplied the same invariant for L1/L2. The contribution also hardened shared recipe-driven dummy generation in `src\winml\modelkit\onnx\io.py`: when `InputTensorSpec.name == "bbox"` and the last dim is 4, reorder coordinates so top-left <= bottom-right before feeding LayoutLM.

findings.title: GELU fusion reduces W8A16 QNN partitioning from 13 contexts to one and yields a 65.2747% paired gain
findings.observation: The optimization run compared the original W8A16 graph with the GELU-fused candidate on the same fixed sample and frozen QNN provider options. Residual Erf operators fell from 12 to 0 and QNN EPContext partitions fell from 13 to 1. Across the confirmed paired A/B/B/A protocol, baseline p50 was 45.443 ms, champion p50 was 15.734 ms, and the paired gain was 65.2747% with 95% confidence interval [65.1316%,65.4115%]. Adding MatMul+Add fusion retained one context but failed the fixed span-correctness gate, so node or context count alone was not accepted as performance evidence.

not_yet_tested_on: other LayoutLM checkpoints with Erf-based GELU partitions

gotchas: This paired optimization timing is separate from tester-v5's exact-recipe timing; report each with its own protocol.
A smaller node count or one context is not sufficient: every representation change still requires the fixed-input numeric and argmax gates.
findings.mechanism_notes: The causal candidate changed GELU representation, eliminated exactly the 12 residual Erf islands, collapsed 13 contexts to one, passed correctness, and then reproduced the latency reduction under paired fresh-session ordering.

findings.title: The one-context W8A16 graph is HTP-saturated and dominated by Add and Softmax work
findings.observation: Complete QNN optrace/QHAS profiling of the one-context W8A16 champion measured graph execute time 15,415 us and HTP utilization 99.861%. Active-cycle shares were ElementWiseAdd 36.208%, Softmax 18.078%, MatMul 11.845%, FullyConnected 10.466%, Gelu 9.895%, and LayerNorm 8.688%. The profile also recorded 168,085,504 DRAM-read bytes, 1,699,840 DRAM-write bytes, and 6,922,240 peak VTCM bytes. BiasSoftmax and AttentionFusion probes were no-ops, so the profile supports bandwidth/kernel tuning rather than another ungrounded graph rewrite.

validated_on: impira/layoutlm-document-qa@beed3c4d02d86017ebca5bd0fdf210046b907aa6 @ one-context W8A16 @ QNN optrace/QHAS @ Snapdragon X Elite
not_yet_tested_on: other samples, sequence lengths, QNN SDK versions, or Snapdragon devices

gotchas: QHAS graph execute time is provider attribution evidence, not interchangeable with process wall-clock latency.
The profile covers one fixed valid sample; do not generalize the exact hotspot shares to all document workloads.
findings.mechanism_notes: The raw optrace log and matching complete schematic produced a 395-node detail trace and an `ok` QHAS summary; HTP utilization and active-cycle categories came from that provider-level trace.

findings.title: QNN/NPU fp32 reverses a narrow start-logit rank during HTP lowering and is an exhausted failure
findings.observation: For fixed sample_01, the PyTorch-derived reference ranks index 0 above index 511 by only 0.000403761864. QNN fp32 changes that margin to -0.0009765625 and changes start argmax 0 -> 511, despite minimum cosine 0.999983828425349 and maximum normalized RMSE 0.006038571607082 over the four-sample corpus. Native-GELU and Erf precompile graphs produced byte-identical QNN outputs, and explicitly setting the documented `enable_htp_fp16_precision=0` option also produced the same hashes. Running the exact optimized graph on CPU preserved argmax 0, a 0.000403165817 margin, and cosine 1.0, isolating the reversal to QNN HTP lowering. The candidate recipe was removed.

falsified_on: the native GELU rewrite is the sole cause of the fp32 rank reversal
enable_htp_fp16_precision=0 restores this checkpoint's fp32 span ordering
not_yet_tested_on: a future QNN/ORT release with different HTP float lowering
real document rows whose best span has a wider logit margin

findings.recipe_template: N/A - the failed fp32 candidate was removed
gotchas: High cosine and low normalized RMSE do not protect extractive QA when the top span logits are nearly tied; retain exact start/end argmax gates.
Do not reopen this precision from static support or graph-shape evidence alone; require new provider/runtime evidence that changes the QNN outputs.
findings.mechanism_notes: The CPU/QNN boundary localizes the defect to provider lowering, and two graph representations plus the direct HTP float-precision option exhausted the bounded in-scope repairs. The specific internal HTP kernel or rounding site remains unidentified.

findings.title: W8A8 calibration changes do not recover LayoutLM span correctness on QNN/NPU
findings.observation: The exact W8A8 QNN/NPU tuple failed the fixed four-sample correctness contract under multiple calibration paths. Default/random calibration reached minimum cosine 0.709118363185076 and maximum normalized RMSE 0.764987022147052, with only sample_03 preserving both span argmaxes. Recalibration over all four valid NPZ inputs still failed every sample, with minimum cosine 0.737270516907190 and maximum normalized RMSE 0.757015889205482. The sparse one-context graph did not repair the error. The candidate recipe was removed and no performance claim was made.

falsified_on: invalid random calibration data is the sole cause of this checkpoint's W8A8 failure
not_yet_tested_on: selective mixed-precision tensor overrides
a larger real-document calibration corpus
future QNN quantization implementations

findings.recipe_template: N/A - the failed W8A8 candidate was removed
gotchas: Do not infer W8A8 support from W8A16; each precision needs an exact artifact and safety verdict.
A successful quantize/compile command does not establish model support when span logits and argmaxes fail.
The model-level precision outcome is `required-tuples-contain-exhausted-failures`, not full or partial coverage; keep fp32 and W8A8 explicit and out of deferred_tuples.
findings.mechanism_notes: The evidence rules out calibration-input validity as the sole cause but does not localize which W8A8 tensor or region destroys span quality. Reopening requires a new bounded repair such as evidenced selective mixed precision, not another equivalent calibration rerun.
